transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-30
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 48 min
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Starlane Head of Cloud), Ben Morales (Platform Eng), Evelyn Zhou (Security)
---
Auto-summary: Quick technical sync to align security and networking for the joint marketplace reference architecture.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have like 45-ish minutes. Quick intro — Maya from Redwood, Liam is our solutions engineer, and from Starlane we have Priya, Ben and Evelyn.
00:12 Speaker 2 (Priya): Hi hi, thanks. We wanted to make sure the network and auth bits are nailed down before we start trying to put the listing into the cloud marketplace.
00:24 Speaker 1 (Maya): Totally. High level agenda: networking options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), auth story (SAML/SSO + token exchange), key management and packaging (helm vs OCI), then pilot plan. Sound ok?
00:35 Speaker 3 (Liam): Yep. I'll start on the networking, try not to be too kubernety, promise.
00:45 Speaker 3 (Liam): So, two main patterns we see — customer VPC peering or PrivateLink/private endpoint. Peering is simple but you need route tables and peer bandwidth, PrivateLink gives you more control and it's easier for regulated customers who don't want cross-account route exposure.
00:58 Speaker 2 (Priya): If we go peering, we have to involve our network team for route table review and propagation— they hate manual routes. Also curious about egress costs.
01:12 Speaker 3 (Liam): Right, egress is a factor. With peering it's usually cheaper on same region but botched if cross-region. PrivateLink can add per-ENI overhead and NLB costs. For the refarch doc we'll call out cost tradeoffs.
01:28 Speaker 4 (Ben): What about transit gateway? We use TGW for multi-account routing, could that sit in the middle?
01:36 Speaker 3 (Liam): Yes TGW is a good middle ground for multi-account orgs. We support that pattern — the only caveat is the extra hop adds 1–3ms median, p99 impact depends on your path. We'll benchmark.
01:52 Speaker 2 (Priya): Ok makes sense. Next auth, Evelyn can you say what Starlane requires?
02:00 Speaker 5 (Evelyn): We need SSO into the console for ops, SAML with OKTA, and for API calls we prefer short-lived tokens from our KMS. Also KMS key ownership — we want customer-managed keys (CMKs) for logs and model input retention.
02:17 Speaker 3 (Liam): We support SAML SSO and have an OIDC token flow for service-to-service. For CMKs we can integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS + external HSM) — we call that out in the private deployment model.
02:33 Speaker 2 (Priya): Are there any gotchas with exchanging tokens between Redwood hosted and our private infra?
02:40 Speaker 3 (Liam): The main one is token audience and scopes. We've seen customers expect opaque tokens but Redwood expects an OIDC JWT with audience redwood:ingest or similar. We can add a small adapter in the flow to accept their tokens if needed. That adapter can be deployed as a sidecar or a lightweight token broker in their VPC.
03:05 Speaker 4 (Ben): Could that broker be open-source? Our infra team prefers to review code.
03:12 Speaker 3 (Liam): Yes, we can provide a reference token broker repo. Will put link in notes.
03:20 Speaker 1 (Maya): Note: link to sample token broker repo: https://git.redwood.example/partner/token-broker (placeholder)
03:30 Speaker 2 (Priya): Great. Can we talk about data residency and logs? We have to keep certain logs within EU region.
03:38 Speaker 3 (Liam): Two options: region pinning on the hosted model and or private deployment in your VPC. Hosted can be region-restricted and logs can be routed to your Kinesis/SQS through a private endpoint. But if you need full control, Private deployment with customer-managed storage is best.
03:56 Speaker 5 (Evelyn): For SOC 2 we need audit trails and immutable logs. Does Redwood support forwarding audit logs to our SIEM?
04:05 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, we have export hooks and can forward to S3 or directly to your SIEM via secure TLS. We also support long-term retention add-ons.
04:18 Speaker 5 (Evelyn): Ok please capture that in the security checklist.
04:25 Speaker 3 (Liam): On packaging — two options: Helm chart that installs the Redwood connector, or an OCI module/sidecar image plus a Terraform module for infra. Helm is quicker for K8s customers; Terraform module is nicer for infra-as-code folks.
04:44 Speaker 4 (Ben): We deploy via Terraform modules across accounts, so a TF module is ideal. But we can also use helm in the staging cluster.
04:53 Speaker 3 (Liam): We'll produce both. Action: we'll publish a sample helm chart and a terraform example.
05:03 Speaker 2 (Priya): Pilot perf plan — we want to measure median latency, p95/p99, and token cost per 1k requests. Also KV cache warmup behavior for conversational workloads.
05:15 Speaker 3 (Liam): Good. For KV cache, note that tuning cache size and TTL has big perf/cost tradeoffs. We'll instrument cache hit rates and token breakdowns. That will feature in the perf runbook.
05:30 Speaker 4 (Ben): On the marketplace listing, we need a reference architecture diagram, a security checklist, and a quickstart. Do you have a template?
05:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, we'll share our partner listing template and a sample refarch diagram. I'll attach that to the notes.
05:49 Speaker 2 (Priya): About model variants — if we want a lower-cost quantized model for non-sensitive workloads, can you do auto-fallback?
05:57 Speaker 3 (Liam): Redwood runtime supports routing policies; you can specify fallback to a cheaper quantized variant. We'll document quality tradeoffs.
06:07 Speaker 2 (Priya): Cool. Any limitations for on-prem/air-gapped?
06:13 Speaker 3 (Liam): On-prem requires an offline bundle and we'll need to ship a prebuilt image. There are kernel/driver dependencies for GPUs; ops needs to validate our supported CUDA/cuDNN versions. We'll add a preflight checklist.
06:28 Speaker 5 (Evelyn): For the preflight we need a security posture checklist — firewall rules, KMS endpoints, image signing verification.
06:36 Speaker 3 (Liam): We'll provide image signing and a checksum manifest. Also recommend customers use ephemeral keys for service accounts.
06:48 Speaker 1 (Maya): Quick check — any blockers from Starlane side right now?
06:53 Speaker 2 (Priya): Timeline: we'd like a pilot within 2 weeks, but security team needs the checklist.
07:00 Speaker 4 (Ben): I'll try to get the test tenant standing up by Friday. Might take a day or two to scrub payloads.
07:07 Speaker 5 (Evelyn): I'll send a short SOC 2 questionnaire to Maya after this call.
07:13 Speaker 1 (Maya): Perfect. We'll follow up with the refarch, helm and tf examples and perf plan.
07:20 Speaker 3 (Liam): One more thing — if you expect sustained high throughput we recommend dedicated capacity. That reduces p99 and gives reserved GPU pools. Pricing/discussion can happen with the GTM team.
07:36 Speaker 2 (Priya): Makes sense. We'll scope the pilot and then decide.
07:42 Speaker 1 (Maya): Ok let's do a quick recap and owners.
07:47 Speaker 1 (Maya): Maya will send the refarch diagram, partner listing template, and sample helm chart and tf module.
07:55 Speaker 4 (Ben): Ben will provision the test tenant and sample traffic.
08:00 Speaker 5 (Evelyn): Evelyn will send SOC 2 scoping questions.
08:05 Speaker 3 (Liam): Liam will put together the perf runbook and KV cache tuning notes.
08:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): We agreed to meet again for pilot kickoff on 2025-07-14, tentative. I'll send calendar invite after this.
08:20 Speaker 2 (Priya): Thanks all.
08:24 Speaker 1 (Maya): Thanks, bye.
